sources.title: USSR Law No. 1360-I, 14 March 1990: creation of the Presidency and constitutional amendments
sources.publisher: USSR Congress of People's Deputies; original law held by GARF, reproduced by Bavarian State Library, 1000 Schluesseldokumente
sources.access_method: Russian original-law transcription read; four GARF facsimile leaves visually inspected

claims.text: The law creates the USSR Presidency; new Article 127 identifies the President as head of the Soviet state.
claims.locator: Section I; Section II.3, Article 127; facsimile pages 1 and 3

claims.text: The law removes the preamble's leading-party sentence and replaces Article 6 with participation by the CPSU, other parties, organizations and movements.
claims.uncertainty: Replacement of wording is not dissolution of the CPSU or proof that every political organization was registered.

claims.text: The first President is elected by the USSR Congress for five years and enters office upon taking the oath; this differs from the new general popular-election rule.
claims.locator: Section III.1-2; Article 127.1; facsimile pages 3 and 14
claims.uncertainty: A statutory selection rule, not evidence of who was elected or when an oath was taken.

claims.text: The dated signature block identifies M. Gorbachev as Chairman of the USSR Supreme Soviet.
claims.locator: Signature and date block; facsimile page 14
claims.uncertainty: One signed office observation; neither a complete chairmanship nor a presidential appointment.

claims.text: Section IV makes the law effective upon adoption. The instrument is dated 14 March 1990 and numbered 1360-I.
claims.locator: Section IV and instrument number/date; facsimile page 14
claims.uncertainty: No later constitutional version or office lifespan is certified by this enactment.

sources.scope_note: Claims use the reproduced primary Russian law, not the separate 2011/2024 scholarly introduction or its political interpretations. The repository cites GARF F. R-9654, Op. 1, D. 121, leaves 22-35 and the 1990 third extraordinary Congress stenographic report, volume 3, pages 192-207. Only facsimile pages 1, 3, 13 and 14 were visually reviewed. The 14 March law date must not become Gorbachev's presidential oath date.

sources.title: Diplomatic Bluebook 1990, Section 4: Soviet Union
sources.access_method: Official HTML text read through web retrieval; separate direct HTTP download returned 403 and was not accepted as source bytes

claims.text: Japan's 1990 diplomatic account reports Gorbachev's election as General Secretary at the July 1990 CPSU congress while separately calling him President.
claims.locator: 1. Internal Politics, (1) Progress in Political Reform, July congress paragraphs
claims.uncertainty: Month-level contemporaneous diplomatic observation; original CPSU election protocol and exact election day were not inspected.

claims.text: The account reports a new Deputy General Secretary office supporting the General Secretary and supervising the Secretariat, with Vladimir Ivashkov elected.
claims.locator: 1. Internal Politics, (1) Progress in Political Reform, last paragraph
claims.uncertainty: The source spells the name Ivashkov; reconciliation with original-language identity and election records is pending. This is not a succession entitlement or a continuous deputy term.

sources.scope_note: A primary record of Japan's contemporary diplomatic reporting, not an original Soviet party register or election instrument. Retain its month precision and the reported Ivashkov spelling. No independent use is made of its shorthand for constitutional powers, its labels for new groups, or its republic-level office descriptions. The edition year is not a known website publication day.

sources.title: Letter from President Bush to Soviet President Gorbachev, 20 March 1990 (FRUS 1989-1992, volume XXXI, document 90)
sources.publisher: United States Department of State, Office of the Historian; George H. W. Bush Presidential Library record
sources.access_method: Official archival diplomatic-letter transcription and source notes read

claims.text: Bush's letter dated 20 March 1990 addresses Gorbachev as President; the editorial transmission note identifies him as USSR President.
claims.locator: Document heading, dated salutation and footnote 3
claims.uncertainty: An office observation in diplomatic correspondence, not the election, oath, term start or proof of continuous service.

sources.scope_note: The archive identifies George H.W. Bush Library, Bush Presidential Records, Brent Scowcroft Collection, Special Separate USSR Notes Files, Gorbachev Files, OA/ID 91126-006. Footnote 3 records Scowcroft's 21 March 0001Z transmission instruction. The letter's 20 March date and the later transmission must remain distinct. No arms-control offer, military capability or outcome is imported into gameplay.

Obtain the later chairman election and full chamber membership records independently.
Keep USSR Congress and Supreme Soviet institutions distinct from the similarly named RSFSR bodies and from political parties.
This is a bounded 1990 source inventory: one party and three state institutions, not an exhaustive USSR party, faction, opposition, republic or coalition census.

The packet does not establish absence of other organizations. Discover original party registers, congresses, candidate organizations and opposition movements with separate union/republic jurisdiction.
Exact party election dates, acting roles, original spelling and full leadership intervals remain unresolved; contemporary Japanese diplomatic reporting is not an original CPSU election protocol.
1991 office changes, emergency claims, resignations, suspensions and dissolution require their own source review. No legal or organizational continuity through 2026 is inferred.
The USSR packet remains separate from Russia. Existing game party mappings, historical avatar eligibility, likeness approval and post-cutoff fictional succession are not changed.
